prompt: What does the `<#>` operator return in pgvector?
code: SELECT * FROM items ORDER BY embedding <#> '[3,1,2]' LIMIT 5;

options.text: The inner product, so larger means more similar.
The negative inner product, because Postgres index scans only support ascending order on operators.

explanation: pgvector supports `<->` (L2), `<#>` (negative inner product), `<=>` (cosine distance) and `<+>` (L1). `<#>` returns the negative inner product so that ascending ORDER BY returns the most similar rows first; multiply by -1 to get the actual inner product.
